profileStatsNoteLead: Not one of them is guessed, and not one of them is the site's to invent. Here is what each figure is, whose it is, and what the site does with it.
profileStatsNoteBlizzardBody: The item level, the character's level, the Mythic+ rating, the achievements and the collection lists are asked of the Armoury itself, character by character. The site shows only what the Blizzard API answered: a figure that has not been read yet, or that is missing from the answer, is drawn as a dash rather than a zero.
profileStatsNoteCatalogueTitle: Counted against everything the game holds
profileStatsNoteCatalogueBody: The complete catalogues of mounts, pets, toys, decor and achievements are gathered in advance and built into the site's own database. That is what lets the system know about every item the game holds, and not only the ones this character has earned - which is how the exact percentage and progress of a collection are formed. Items the game has retired, and content it has not shipped yet, are left out by default; the two switches in the collections menu turn them on.
profileStatsNoteScopeBody: In World of Warcraft most collections are tied to a Battle.net account, and the site marks which is which on every card: mounts, pets, toys, decor, achievements and reputations are counted across the whole account - the site unites the unique items and factions of every character you have read it with, reputations including the factions of both sides. The Mythic+ rating, the item level and the character's level, in turn, stay the chosen hero's own.
profileStatsNoteScoreTitle: The gold figure is the site's own score
profileStatsNoteScoreBody: The score is formed from the collection alone, every category carrying a weight of its own: a mount 25, a toy 15, a pet or a piece of decor 5, a reputation taken to its maximum 50, an achievement point 1. The "?" beside the column headings in the Hall of Fame opens a tooltip with those multipliers, read straight from the live code. The M+ rating and the item level are deliberately not part of this score, because they reflect the gear worn today rather than a gathered collection.
profileStatsNoteFreshBody: A character's data is asked of Blizzard once and kept in a local database, which is why the site's pages open instantly. When the last request was made is always shown under the block of buttons ("Updated"). Refresh re-requests the current character, Update all sends a request across your whole roster, and the global Hall of Fame table is rebuilt automatically once an hour.
profileStatsNotePublicBody: Only your main character appears in the Hall of Fame; every other alt stays inside the profile and is hidden from strangers. The "Hall of Fame" switch in the settings can hide even the main from the overall ranking. The green dot on a character's portrait in the table means the owner of that account is on the site at this moment.

privacyMeta: What the site collects, and what it does not
privacySeoDescription: What Hero of Azeroth collects: the characters read through Blizzard's APIs, what signing in with Battle.net stores, and how Google Analytics is used.
privacyWhatTitle: What does Hero of Azeroth collect?
privacyWhatBody:
Hero of Azeroth collects information about the names, progress, achievements and in-game collectables of virtual characters within World of Warcraft. All of it is publicly available on the World of Warcraft Armoury, and none of it is tied to or correlated with any real-world information.

The site does not ask visitors for any personal information, and a visitor who never signs in leaves nothing behind.
privacySigninBody:
Signing in is optional, and it is the only thing here with an account behind it. The site never sees the password: it is typed on Blizzard's own page, and what comes back is the account's id, its BattleTag and the list of characters that account leads with.

Your profile decides what is published. The main you name appears in the Hall of Fame with its figures, and its alts are stored beside it. The profile's switch for the Hall of Fame can be set to do not publish, which takes the whole account out of the table - and the same rows are deleted on request, in Telegram.
privacyAnalyticsBody: The site counts visits with Google Analytics, which runs through Google Tag Manager. Nothing is stored on your device until you allow it in the cookie question at the foot of the page; if you decline, the counter keeps counting anonymously - no cookies, and nothing that identifies you. What Google does with what it collects is covered by Google's own privacy policy.
privacyHowBody:
Character information is read through the web APIs Blizzard Entertainment publishes for the game, and only for characters somebody has looked up: the site knows the characters it has been asked about, and nothing else.

Some of what a page shows comes straight from other people's servers - the portraits and backgrounds from Blizzard's media service, the item tooltips from Wowhead's script. Like any script or image on any site, those requests carry the visitor's IP address to those services.
privacyStoreTitle: How is it stored and protected?
privacyStoreBody: Whatever is collected is stored on the server this site runs on, in its own database, and nowhere else. The site follows the ordinary practices for keeping data away from people who should not have it: HTTPS in transit, a firewall, strong passwords and routine rotation of the keys.
privacyAccessBody: Nothing about characters, accounts or visitors is sold or shared with third parties. What Google Analytics collects is covered by Google's own policy, and nothing else leaves the site.
privacyUpdateBody: This policy is updated as needed, mainly to stay in step with Blizzard Entertainment's own policies. Updates are posted on this page, with a new date at the top.
aboutMeta: A free fan site for World of Warcraft players and collectors
aboutSeoDescription: Hero of Azeroth is a free World of Warcraft fan site: a character card, collections of mounts, pets and toys, achievements, reputations, character comparison and a shared Hall of Fame.
aboutTagline: Your journey through Azeroth, in one character card
aboutLead: Hero of Azeroth brings a character's progress together in one place - item level and Mythic+ rating, collections, achievements and reputations - and turns it into a card you can share.
aboutIntro:
A World of Warcraft character's progress is scattered across a dozen places: collections in the journal, achievements in their own tab, a Mythic+ rating in another window, and alts on realms you have to remember. Putting that together - and showing it to somebody - takes time, especially when what you want to show is a character rather than a number.

Hero of Azeroth gathers it in one place: a character's page with their figures, a card worth sharing, and a table where you can see how they compare. Collectors have something worth showing: a rare mount farmed for months, a difficult achievement, a reputation carried to the end on more than one character. The site makes that progress visible - and keeps the items still missing the easiest thing to see.

It is built for the community: look up your own character, look up somebody else's, compare with friends and your guild, and see what is left to collect. It is free, has no advertising, and is still growing.
aboutFeatureCardsBody: A character's page becomes an image with their portrait and their headline figures: item level, Mythic+ rating, achievement points and collection totals. Download it or drop it into Discord - a link to the character shows that same card wherever previews are supported.
aboutFeatureCollectorsBody: Mounts, pets, toys and decor: what is already collected, what is missing, and how much of the journal is left. Collections and reputations can be read for the character or for the whole Battle.net account, because the game shares many of them across every character.
aboutFeatureAchievementsBody: Achievement points by category and a feed of the ones earned most recently, plus every reputation with its standing. Reputations are counted the way the game counts them: a character's own, and the account's union across the roster.
aboutFeatureCompareBody: Two characters side by side: item level, Mythic+ rating, collections and the rest of the figures, row by row. Where the site has history and readings from other players, a chart and a distribution are drawn beside them, so you can see where a figure stands.
aboutFeatureFameBody: One shared table, ranked by an overall score built from achievements, mounts, pets, toys, decor and reputations, and a ranking for each figure on its own. It holds the characters the site has already read, and an account is counted across its whole roster - so what the alts gathered is never counted twice.
aboutFeatureDashboardBody: Signing in is optional and happens on Blizzard's side - the password is typed there and never reaches the site. Once signed in you get the roster, you name a main (the main is what represents the account in the table), the account's totals are added up, and the account can be taken out of the Hall of Fame entirely.
aboutPrincipleFree: Free: no paid tiers, no subscriptions, nothing held back.
aboutPrincipleNoAds: No advertising: no banners and no ad slots on any page.
aboutPrincipleIndependent: Independent: not affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment and not endorsed by it.
aboutPrincipleSources: Character data is read through the sources Blizzard publishes for the game, and only for the characters somebody has looked up.
aboutPrincipleAnalytics: The visitor counter is optional: if you decline analytics, Google Analytics keeps counting visits without cookies or identifiers, and the advertising signals stay off either way.
aboutPrincipleEvolving: The site keeps growing: new sections and figures are added, and speed and readability are always being worked on.
legalMeta: Who owns World of Warcraft, and where the site's data comes from
legalSeoDescription: Hero of Azeroth is a free, non-commercial World of Warcraft fan site: game artwork and trademarks belong to their respective rights holders, the site is not affiliated with Blizzard Entertainment, and character data is read through Blizzard's official Web API.
legalAboutBody: Hero of Azeroth is a free, non-commercial fan project, made by players for the World of Warcraft community. Nothing on the site is for sale, and there is no advertising on it.
legalOwnershipBody:
World of Warcraft, Warcraft, Battle.net and Blizzard Entertainment are trademarks of Blizzard Entertainment, Inc. Game artwork, images and other rights connected with the game belong to their respective rights holders.

The site claims neither them nor the game data: it only shows what is already published for players.
legalIndependentBody:
Hero of Azeroth is not created, affiliated with, endorsed or supported by Blizzard Entertainment.

Questions and corrections about the site go to its author rather than to Blizzard.
legalSourcesBody:
Character information is read through Blizzard's official Web API - the details the game publishes about characters, their collections and their reputations. It is read only for the characters somebody has looked up: the site knows nothing about a character nobody has opened.

Some of what a page shows comes from other people's services: character portraits and background artwork from Blizzard's media service, and item and achievement icons and tooltips from Wowhead (ZamImg). As on any site, those requests carry the visitor's IP address to those services.

The catalogue of collectable items the collections are counted against is assembled from publicly published community data, and refreshed after new versions of the game ship.
